name: GitHub
summary: The largest code host: Git repositories, pull requests, issues, Actions and the social graph of open source.

factors: Issues, pull requests and review history live outside the Git repository
Actions workflows and the marketplace actions they depend on
The community: stars, followers, drive-by contributors and 'Sign in with GitHub'
Integrations that assume GitHub: bots, deploy hooks, package registries, Pages

export.summary: Git history moves with one command. Issues, pull requests, releases and wikis are reachable through the API, and both forges below import them for you.

methods.name: git clone --mirror
methods.detail: Copies every branch, tag and ref. This is the part that can never be locked in.

methods.name: Built-in importers
methods.detail: Forgejo and GitLab both pull a repository together with its issues, pull requests, labels, milestones and releases, using a personal access token.

methods.name: Migration archives
methods.detail: GitHub can produce an archive of an organisation's or user's repositories and metadata as JSON, which is useful for safekeeping.

caveats: API rate limits make very large repositories slow to import
Imported comments are attributed to the importing account unless matching users exist on the new forge
Actions secrets, branch protection rules and webhooks must be recreated
Git LFS objects need a separate fetch and push
Stars, watchers and forks stay behind; consider leaving a read-only mirror that points to the new home

paths.verdict: The best fit for small teams and open-source projects that want something light and community-governed.

import.summary: New Migration → GitHub, paste a token and tick what to bring: issues, pull requests, labels, milestones, releases and wiki. Workflow files need reviewing, because Forgejo Actions is similar to GitHub Actions rather than identical.

transfers: Full Git history, branches and tags
Issues, pull requests, labels, milestones and releases
lost: Workflows that rely on GitHub-hosted runners or GitHub-specific actions

paths.verdict: For teams that want the most complete built-in CI/CD and are prepared to give it serious hardware.

import.summary: GitLab's GitHub importer brings repositories with issues, pull requests (as merge requests), comments, labels, milestones and releases. The larger job is rewriting Actions workflows as GitLab CI pipelines.

transfers: Full Git history, branches and tags
Issues, pull requests, comments, labels, milestones and releases
lost: Every Actions workflow, which must be rewritten
Features that are free on GitHub but paid on GitLab, such as some approval rules
